summary: Strong, well-sourced file. All CFC/CPAS rates (PT 03-25, rate disclosure, FY2027 'level rates'), all six BLS OEWS May 2025 Maryland wages, CareScout $35/hr, COMAR 10.07.05 fees/terms/RN supervision/on-call, COMAR 10.09.84 provider conditions, MPRIME dates/phone, UI/FAMLI/mileage/CMS fee/SDAT fees and the OHCQ, OLTSS and MPRIME phone numbers were verified against primary sources. The model recomputes exactly as the narrative states (mix100 +$11,806 at 0.629 break-even occupancy; mix60 +$3,632; med100 +$2,035; pp30 +$178; med60 -$810; med30 -$6,775), and the sensitivity, startup and ramp figures match. One critical error: the Montgomery County wage exception for Medicaid-funded home care requires at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid, so the mixed configurations (default mix100 is ~65% Medicaid revenue; mix60 ~74%) owe the $18.00 large-employer minimum there, which roughly halves the default result. The other issues are a dead ISAS URL, a mislabeled lease override, source_id mismatches and small wording points.

issues.current: Montgomery County: 'Medicaid-funded home care employers with 11+ employees fall in the $16.50 mid-size tier... The modeled Medicaid aide wage of $17.06 clears every floor. A private-pay Montgomery agency with 51+ employees... must pay at least $18.00.'
issues.correct: The mid-size ($16.50) tier applies to a home care provider with 11+ employees only if it 'receives at least 75% of gross revenues through state and federal Medicaid programs.' The default mix100 (60% Medicaid clients) earns about 64.6% of revenue from Medicaid ($1,535 of $2,375 per client-month) and mix60 about 74.0% ($1,791 of $2,421), so in Montgomery County a mixed agency with 51+ employees must pay at least $18.00 to all aides. Recomputed at $18.00 for Medicaid aides: mix100 = +$5,464/month (2.6% margin, break-even 75 clients / 0.75 occupancy; +$1,817 at 80% census); mix60 = -$808/month (break-even 56.5 clients). Medicaid-only configs (100% Medicaid revenue) do qualify for $16.50.
issues.evidence: Maryland Department of Labor wage page: Montgomery County from July 1, 2026 — large (51+) $18.00, mid-sized (11-50) $16.50, small $15.95; 'Certain non-profits and Medicaid-funded home care providers are subject to the mid-sized rate even if they employ more than 51 employees... must have 11 or more employees and... receives at least 75% of gross revenues through state and federal Medicaid programs.' Recomputed with generators/model.py by setting the $17.06 Medicaid-aide wage to $18.00 in mix60/mix100.
issues.fix: In market_conditions, risks #2, the Montgomery bullet and the financial_narrative sensitivity add: 'The $16.50 tier applies only if at least 75% of gross revenue comes from Medicaid. A mixed agency like the default (about 65% Medicaid revenue) with 51+ employees must pay $18.00 in Montgomery County; at $18.00 the 100-client mixed agency nets about +$5,464 a month (2.6%, break-even 75 clients) and the 60-client mixed agency about -$808.' Replace 'The modeled Medicaid aide wage of $17.06 clears every floor' with 'clears every floor except Montgomery County for agencies under 75% Medicaid revenue with 51+ employees.' In recommendations #6 add the 75% test.
